title: Cookie API

labels.name: needs implementer interest
labels.description: Moving the issue forward requires implementers to express interest

body:
### What problem are you trying to solve?

## 1. Manipulating cookies

Historically, manipulating cookies in JavaScript has been tedious. Client-side cookies are represented in a single `document.cookie` string (requiring parsing), and server-side cookies have no standard representation, to begin with. 

As a JavaScript developer, I want a standard and straightforward API to 1) create, and 2) manipulate cookies in JavaScript. 

## 2. Declaring server-side cookies

Modern JavaScript development is in the transition to a complete client/server collocation. This means more and more developers will get familiarized with and be working with things like cookies on a daily basis. Having a standard API to manage cookies would be beneficial to those developers and reduce the dependency cost when working with cookies.

## 3. Declaring cookies in mocks

I'm coming from the API mocking environment, where working with client-side and server-side cookies is natural. I want the users of my software to have the ability to work with cookies in a standardized way, given that 1) the cookie specification is clear; 2) the existing third-party solutions have already cultivated the expectations toward working with cookies. 

## 4. Representational problem

At its core, representing and working with cookies as _strings_ is inefficient. That feels like the implementation detail of the platform, if I may. As a developer, I want a concise and functional abstraction that would help me create and manipulate cookies while I develop JavaScript applications. 

### What solutions exist today?

The demand for cookie string manipulation has been historically high. This spawned a number of third-party packages ([one](https://www.npmjs.com/package/cookie), [two](https://www.npmjs.com/package/set-cookie-parser), [three](https://www.npmjs.com/package/cookie-parser)) with dozens of millions of downloads in total. Natively, JavaScript provides no solution to working with cookies, which is precisely what this proposal aims to solve.

### How would you solve it?

By introducing a new `Cookie` API. 

## API


```ts
class Cookie {
  public name: string
  public value: string
  public domain: string | undefined
  public path: string | undefined
  public maxAge: number | undefined
  public expires: Date | undefined
  public secure: boolean
  public httpOnly: boolean
  public sameSite: 'strict' | 'lax' | 'none' | undefined
  public partitioned: boolean

  // Parse a cookie string into a Cookie instance.
  static parse(input: string): Cookie {}

  // Serialize the given Cookie instances into a single cookie string.
  static serialize(...cookies: Cookie[]): string {}

  // Create a new cookie instance.
  constructor(name: string, value: string, options?: CookieOptions) {}

  public isExpired(): boolean

  // Serialize this Cookie instance to a valid cookie string.
  public toString(): string
}
```

The `Cookie` API is designed to solve the following problems:

1. Provide a straightforward way to _create_ cookies. This includes manual creation using the `Cookie` constructor, or creating a cookie object from an existing cookie string via the `Cookie.parse()` static method.
2. Serialize existing cookies into _cookie strings_. 
3. Manipulating cookies. This includes checking their values, expiration date, and other properties in order to build the correct logic around cookies (e.g. authentication, authorization, mocking). 

The proposed API **is not** designed to handle the following problems:

1. Setting cookies on the `document`.
2. Collecting cookies (see `CookieStore` for that).
3. Anything else but simple parse/serialize operations on the cookie string. 

## Usage example

### Simple example

```js
const cookie = new Cookie('session', 'value', { expires: new Date('2024-01-01') })
cookie.name // "session"
cookie.value // "value"
cookie.isExpired() // false

cookie.toString() // "session=value; Expires=Mon, 01 Jan 2024 00:00:00 GMT"
```

### Server-side cookie

The proposed `Cookie` API can also be used to declare cookies in server-side environments,  such as in modern JavaScript frameworks like Remix and Next (which ship their own abstractions to achieve that), or in API mocking tools like MSW.

```js
http.post('/login', ({ request }) => {
  const sessionCookie = new Cookie('session', 'secret', {
    expires: Date.now + day,
    httpOnly: true,
    secure: true
  })

  return new Response(null, {
    status: 301,
    headers: {
      'Set-Cookie': sessionCookie.toString(),
      Location: '/dashboard',
    }
  })
})
```

### Client-side cookies

In the browser, all cookies are stored in a single `document.cookie` string. Given the multi-value nature of that string, using the proposed `Cookie` API to manipulate `document.cookie` is not efficient in the current state of the proposal. I believe this particular use case either requires a new API or can utilize the existing experimental `CookieStore` API (if the said API is intended to be used that way, of course). 

### Anything else?

Upon a brief discussion of this proposal on [Twitter](https://twitter.com/kettanaito/status/1724830073566429211), some developers voiced concerns about the [`CookieStore` API](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/CookieStore). I'd like to emphasize that the `CookieStore` API addresses an entirely different problem and does not substitute the `Cookie` API I'm proposing here. Moreover, one can _combine_ both APIs for handling cookies. 

```js
const store = new CookieStore()
const sessionCookie = new Cookie('session', 'value')

store.set(sessionCookie)
```

> Granted, that requires changes to the experimental `CookieStore` API so I'm listing this here purely for illustrational purposes. 

`CookieStore` methods are _asynchronous_, which is the direct reflection of a different problem that API attempts to solve. The proposed `Cookie` API is meant to be _synchronous_ as it aims to ease the experience of _cookie string manipulation_.
